I can help with the Warcraft III Chimaera: balance reasons. The Chimaera can only target ground with its primary attack, lightning bolts with Magic-type damage (200% damage against most melee ground units, 125% damage against air units, but it cannot hit units with Spell Immunity) but it also has a corrosive breath as a secondary attack that targets buildings with Siege-type damage (150% damage to buildings and most spellcaster units), and both of them deal huge damage. There's no other unit with this combination of traits. If it also attacked air it'd be too powerful. The other air units that have a Siege-type attack are the Orc Bat Rider (only has a Siege-type attack which can target any unit), and the Human Flying Machine (also has a Piercing-type attack that can only target air units, and deals 200% against them), which have no Magic-type attack, and have low HP and Armor.

In short, the Chimaera has effective attacks against melee ground units and buildings, the Bat Rider only against buildings (but it can suicide against other air units for huge damage), and the Flying Machine against buildings and air units. None of them are effective against all three. The other air units are all weak against buildings (both Magic and Piercing-type attacks deal only 35% damage to them). Also, all air units are weak to common ranged ground units.
It gives the early adopter of air warfare an advantage until the first opponent discovers it.
And what about the later game air units that continue to be this way?

Real life examples of what you're questioning would be the A10 Warthog and AC-130 Spectre gunship. They do a really good job of demolishing things on the ground and that's about it.

If you've got units in an RTS that fly and only attack ground units, then you use them when the enemy has ground units and little/no defense against air. If the enemy has air defenses, then you use something else. Not every unit in an RTS has to be viable in every situation or viable throughout a scenario.
Harassment and early scouts. Send a cheap air unit to harass a remote resource point.

It's an easy way to balance a game, you build units in sets of 3s. Each unit beats another unit, so players that focus too heavily on one type can be countered. Rock, paper, scissors... Horse, spear, sword...

The 3s don't have to all be flying units. Anti-Air Ground Units can beat Air to Air, Air to Air can beat Air to Ground, and Air to Ground can beat Anti-Air Ground Units.

Ground units that cannot attack air units are powerless against them, so it's a tool for harassment if there are unguarded ground units or the opponent doesn't have air units yet. Beyond that, probably not a lot of point unless there are extra advantages like the Zerg Guardian being able to snipe from out of the range of common anti air fixtures.

They're semi-bombers. Not as powerful with a single attack/bombing run like true bombers, but in turn they don't have to return to base after every attack.
